data.narrative:
Valar Atomics is a Series B nuclear energy company currently valued at $6.0B post-money, having raised $1.0B to date. The valuation assessment draws on a peer universe of 11 comparable companies across the nuclear energy sector—3 public companies (Oklo, Nano Nuclear Energy, and other SMR-focused firms) and 8 private firms including Helion, X-Energy, Fuse Energy, and others in the same valuation tier.

Two triangulation methods inform the analysis. Stage-progression analysis applies a typical Series B-to-next-stage multiplier of 1.9x to the $6.0B base, yielding $11.4B. Peer-median analysis across the 3 most comparable same-sector companies—Helion ($15.5B, Series F), Oklo ($7.0B, public), and X-Energy ($5.6B, IPO)—produces a median valuation of $7.0B, with a range of $5.6B to $15.5B reflecting stage dispersion in the comps set.

These methods converge on a triangulated valuation range of $6.0B (low) to $13.1B (high), with a median estimate of $9.2B. The current $6.0B valuation sits near the low end, implying meaningful upside under stage-progression assumptions but modest upside relative to the peer median. Key uncertainties include the heterogeneity of the peer set (which spans from Series F to public stage) and the relative maturity of Valar's technology versus comparable firms.
